presenceNote: An archaeological culture, not a tribe: platform-mound towns that archaeologists group as Mississippian, about AD 1000–1700, in western and south-central Kentucky. Drawn: eight whole Kentucky counties holding named towns and mound centers. A general area, not a boundary; no site locations are shown. Medium confidence (years medium, area medium-low).
overlapNote: The Caborn-Welborn villages (about 1400–1700, Union and Henderson counties) are a separate late Mississippian group, drawn separately; Fort Ancient villages lie to the east. The year slider keeps shapes from different centuries apart. No descent from or link to any later people is claimed.
basis: Kentucky Archaeological Survey / Kentucky Heritage Council Mississippi-period chapter and Wikipedia (Mississippian culture). Public agency sources.

legend.label: Approximate general area of Mississippian western Kentucky: 8 Kentucky counties (whole counties, not a boundary)

eras.label: 1000–1700 CE · western and south-central Kentucky
eras.text: Mississippian is an archaeological culture, a group of sites that archaeologists define from the pottery, village layouts and dates they share; it is not a tribe, and no descent from or link to any later people is claimed. The Kentucky Archaeological Survey dates the Mississippi period to about AD 1000–1700 and covers the Purchase, Green River and Upper Cumberland regions and part of the Salt River region. The tint is eight whole Kentucky counties named for documented towns and mound centers (Ballard, Carlisle, Fulton, Marshall, Crittenden, Butler, Logan, Knox). The chapter gives no county list for the culture, so this is a general area, not a boundary, and it is drawn for these site counties only; no site locations are shown. The Caborn-Welborn villages near the mouth of the Wabash (about 1400–1700) are shown separately.
